properties.decision: The distinction req:skill-adherence-is-measured offered is REAL, and it is drawn here: dec:loop-status-state-not-history governs what the LOOP may reason from when it computes debt, and adoption data may never enter that computation. It does not forbid the KIT reporting a fact about itself. Three things make the line enforceable rather than promised: (1) adoption is counted in SESSION state — the hook's per-session tally file — and in transcripts read offline, never in the design graph, so it is not graph state and cannot be reasoned from as if it were; (2) no adoption field is read by loop_status, detect_gaps or detect_defects; (3) a check asserts that the loop's answer is UNCHANGED whether or not adoption data exists, which is what converts the separation from a convention into a property. The test to apply to any future addition: does this measurement ever change what the loop says is owed? If yes, it is forbidden regardless of what it is called.
properties.name: The kit may report its own adoption, because adoption never reaches the debt computation — and a test holds that line rather than a promise
properties.rationale:
WHY THE DISTINCTION IS NOT A RATIONALISATION, which is what the requirement asked to be settled. dec:loop-status-state-not-history exists to protect ONE thing: the answer to "what does this design still need?" must not depend on who did what. If debt read run history, two identical designs would owe different things because their session logs differ, and the design would stop being the single source of truth. That is the harm, and it is specific. Adoption answers a different question, for a different reader, with a different consequence — "is the TOOL being used as intended?", read by the maintainer, changing the TOOL. It never touches the protected answer. So the distinction is not "a different name for the same thing"; it is a different question that happens to be answered from the same kind of evidence, and the decision constrains the QUESTION rather than the evidence.

THE PRECEDENT ALREADY EXISTS AND WAS FOUND RATHER THAN INVENTED. tools/surface_usage.py has done exactly this since 2026-08-01: it reads session transcripts offline, counts get_skill calls among them, and states in its own module docstring that it "writes nothing back into any design — 'looking is not writing' (dec:loop-status-state-not-history). Nothing here becomes graph state." So the shape this decision blesses was already shipping and already reasoned; what was missing was the ruling that makes it deliberate rather than incidental, and a place for the near-real-time half.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY BUILT UNDER IT, and why it is small. The measurement half largely existed. The hole named by chg:undefer-skill-adherence-measurement is different and narrower: cap:skill-triggers recognises SHAPES, every shape it knows is a shape in the graph-write stream, and "no skill has been loaded" is not a graph write — so the one situation the user kept having to correct by hand was the one situation the mechanism structurally could not see. Counting get_skill per session closes that, and it is session state by nature.

THE COST THIS ACCEPTS, stated because the file it lands in resists exactly this. A new arming branch is a NEW interruption, and ver:skill-triggers' own counterweight says a trigger that fires on correct work is the failure BL-23 and BL-42 both name. So the branch is placed LAST, after every other Stop branch has declined, and is conjoined tightly: the session must have TOUCHED reflow2 (a total bypass is already caught upstream), must have edited at least the bypass threshold of files (so a trivial or read-only session is silent), and must have loaded ZERO skills. It therefore fires only on the session that did everything else right and still never opened a skill — which is precisely the case a human had to catch, twice, by asking.

WHAT IS NOT CLAIMED. This measures LOADING, not FOLLOWING. An agent can call get_skill and ignore every word of it, and nothing here would know. Adherence in the strong sense stays unmeasured, and the requirement's name should not be read as claiming otherwise. The honest claim is that not-loading is now visible where it was invisible.

BOUNDARY CARRIED FORWARD from the requirement, unchanged: whatever is reported respects report-friction's redaction discipline — tool names and argument SHAPES, node TYPES not ids, counts not contents — because reflow2 installs into other people's projects and the thing being measured is the user, not their design.

Approved by Anthony 2026-08-07 ("yes, build it") against the recommendation as stated, after he asked for the question in plain terms. The prior "yes, build it" of 2026-08-06 un-deferred the requirement; this settles the precondition it carried.
